newsitem.title: USA: Hotel buyers arrested for taking bribes.
newsitem.headline: Hotel buyers arrested for taking bribes.

text.p: Two senior buyers for ITT Sheraton Corp. were arrested on Monday on charges of taking kickbacks in exchange for buying millions of dollars worth of food supplies for Sheraton hotels, the U.S. Attorney's Office announced.

Starting in 1987 or earlier, Richard Nicoletti and Anthony Giano let Loi Industries Inc., of Englewood, N.J., supply New York and New Jersey Sheraton hotels with produce and eventually meat, orange juice, bread and ice cream, the complaint said.
In exchange Giano and Nicoletti received a kickback of 4 percent of the sales, which amounted to hundreds of thousands of dollars, the FBI and IRS learned from a former Loi employee.
The scheme eventually included Loi selling supplies to Madison Square Garden for a 4 percent kickback, the complaint said.
When Loi went out of business in 1994, the former employee took over Loi's end of the deal for 2 percent kickback, the complaint said.
The complaint said the payments were received under a Sheraton office door or in the bathroom of the "Palm Too" restaurant, which is famous for its cartoon wall drawings.
If convicted the men face up to five years in jail and $250,000 fines for charges of commercial bribery involving interstate travel.
A Sheraton spokeswoman said they were investigating the complaint and declined further comment.
